title: Opaque xN repeat cells are rejected for Observer raw timeline
summary: The standalone ×N repeat-cell experiment is rejected. Raw Unified Timeline must remain literal evidence; repetition may be compacted only when the UI names what was grouped and preserves drill-down.
claims: Standalone ×N markers hide which events were grouped and make the row/grid harder to read.
Raw Unified Timeline is evidence and should remain literal when semantic meaning cannot be preserved.
Semantic compaction belongs in trace/span/expandable summaries, not as an unexplained extra column.
Acceptable summaries name the grouping, e.g. polling for 42s, 3 identical permission failures, or one lifecycle span with state and elapsed time.
decision: Do not reintroduce opaque repeat counters in the raw timeline. Implement named semantic grouping with explicit drill-down or show the raw events.
rationale: Operator comprehension is more important than reducing row count. Compression that removes provenance or meaning is worse than noise.

evidence.note: Architecture rule now explicitly rejects opaque ×N cells.
OBS-07 now carries the rejected-pattern rule and replacement semantics.
